# Folio 1.0-beta3

Linux amd64 prerelease. The supported managed-application platform remains
Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 with systemd. This version includes the beta2 runtime fixes
and the mainline managed database web-tool implementation.

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Aoody743/Folio/releases/download/1.0-beta3/install-1.0-beta3.sh | sudo bash
```

The bootstrap verifies SHA-256 before installation, enables reviewed software
and website modules on a fresh install, and preserves existing Agent policies
on upgrades. Use `--no-managed-features` to opt out of fresh module setup.

## Changes

- Remove the fixed two-GiB website backup/restore and four-GiB database backup
  size ceilings. Authenticated streaming downloads and range/chunk offsets also
  accept larger owned backups. Integrity, path, ownership and bounded-memory
  checks remain in force.
- Require HTTP 2xx/3xx for application startup readiness by default. Applications
  can configure a local check path, expected status codes and a 1–300 second
  startup deadline. Failed startup checks stop the application and report failure.
- Allow `managed_database_backup` in scheduled actions through the shared web,
  REST and MCP registry.
- Persist the associated task ID and reconcile actual success, failure,
  cancellation and interruption into schedule history, including after restart.
  Add optional failure notifications, overlap policies and missed-run policies.
  The panel shows recent outcomes and links to the associated task.
- Add one current release/acceptance entry point; preserve older evidence as
  version-specific history rather than presenting it as current acceptance.

## Acceptance boundaries

See `docs/rewrite/CURRENT-RELEASE.md` and the beta3 acceptance record for the
checks performed on this candidate. This beta does not add verified Debian/ARM
support. Real DNS-provider/public-CA acceptance remains deferred. phpMyAdmin and
pgAdmin adapters are implemented but their declared Debian host workflows remain
experimental and unaccepted; they are not part of the supported Ubuntu matrix.
Private Git authentication remains unsupported.

The removed limits concern owned backup artifacts. Per-request/chunk bounds,
external import parsers, operation deadlines and available disk space still
apply. A notification submission is distinct from final recipient delivery.
